generated_queries.text: Lesson objective: Students will listen to a story read aloud, identify and describe characters and setting, answer questions about key details, participate in role-play to understand major events and central message, and write responses about the story.

Students communicate clearly to present ideas, information, and texts aloud to audiences and peers using spoken language and sentence frames. Standard skill: present ideas information texts clearly in oral communication.

Students make and track predictions about events and information likely to come next in a text based on titles, illustrations, and what they have already read. Standard skill: make and track predictions about upcoming events.
Students engage in dialogue with audiences by asking and answering questions during discussion and close read-aloud. Standard skill: ask and answer questions in oral dialogue with peers.
Students refer to parts of texts when supporting an idea, answer, or opinion. Standard skill: use specific parts of texts to support ideas and answers.

Students describe characters, settings, and major events in a story using key details; describe traits of the main characters and how their words and actions support the central message of the story. Standard skill: describe story structure and character traits with details.
Students learn / practice: identify the main character of a story
Students learn / practice: describe the setting using story details
Students learn / practice: answer questions about key details from a story
Students learn / practice: write responses using pictures and words to show thinking about story elements
Students learn / practice: use sentence frames to support writing about story details
Students learn / practice: participate in role-play to act out major events of a story
Required student action — recognition_identification: Students identify characters and settings in the story and recognize story elements on charts and response sheets.
Required student action — oral_production: Students orally describe characters and settings, answer questions, share out with the group, participate in role-play, and sing the song with motions.

Required student action — written_production: Students write responses to prompts about the main character and setting using pictures and words, and write sentences explaining their word choice with support from sentence frames.
Required student action — procedural_application: Students apply the Role-Play protocol to act out story events and use sentence frames to write about story details.
Vocabulary targets (acquire / apply / clarify meaning): character, setting, central message (L)
Discussion Prompt: Students explain why they chose certain words to describe the character using evidence from pictures and discuss the central message of the story.

Reading Task: Students respond to questions about key details, describe story elements, and reflect on their learning progress using the Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol and group discussion about learning targets and next steps in learning progressions, orally and in writing as appropriate for the task and support provided.
Discussion Prompt: Direct students' attention to the Sun Movement chart and invite a student volunteer to lead the class through one round of the Sun Movement routine.
Discussion Prompt: 'Who is the main character of this story? How would you describe the character?' (Kitten; curious, adventurous, brave, a cat with white fur)
Writing Task: Invite students to complete Part I of the Unit 1 Assessment response sheet. Remind them that they should use pictures and words to show their thinking.

Writing Task: Direct students' attention to the blank lines in Part II. Tell students to write one or two sentences to describe how Kitten is acting and to explain what, from the pictures, helped them.

Reading Task: 'After rereading and acting out these parts of the text, what do you notice about the moon in this story?' (Kitten thinks it is a bowl of milk and she tries to get it, but she can't. The moon stays in the same place the whole time.)
